clue.text: Lace tunic made to impress

indicators.note: made here means fashioned or reworked, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fashions a tunic of lace to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is the anagram signal working on LACE TUNIC; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To inculcate an idea is to fix or stamp it on someone's mind by repetition.

clue.text: Sang when upset

explanation.surface: A singer is put out of tune by emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for informed to the police (a nark is an informer) and British slang for annoyed or irritated.

clue.text: An end to push being used

indicators.note: letters being used are worked over and reshaped, so the words to and push are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gives a final shove to finish a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being used' signals the anagram of TO PUSH; the definition is 'An end'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or final result of a course of events.

clue.text: Rush job?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a hurried task counts as work.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash headlong at speed, and a profession followed through life.

clue.text: Add gold to the list and there'll be a scene!

parts.note: a table is a list of figures set out in rows
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An exclamation that adding gold to a list will cause a dramatic fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Add ... to' sets the order of the pieces; 'scene' means a posed living picture, not a stage setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque grouping, a still scene posed by actors.

clue.text: Popular with a top man on the whole

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a general is a senior military commander

explanation.surface: A well-liked senior officer who is broadly approved of.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean speaking broadly, taking matters overall.

clue.text: Not yet a partner, but standing by

parts.note: later means at a time not yet come
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: Someone not yet made a partner still loyally stands alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing by' means positioned beside, i.e. sideways on.
explanation.definitionFit: Laterally means at the side, as one standing by or beside something stands.

clue.text: American women's team making a strong attack

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman; the possessive gives no letter
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A US women's sports team mounting a powerful offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a full volley from a warship's guns, hence a fierce verbal onslaught.

clue.text: A French blonde is biased

parts.note: un is the French for a
fair means light-haired, blonde

explanation.surface: A French blonde woman shows prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing favouritism rather than even-handed justice.

clue.text: Damn no amateur writer

parts.note: a pro or professional is no amateur
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A professional author is condemned, or an exasperated curse at one.
explanation.definitionFit: To condemn or forbid outright, banning as dangerous.

clue.text: Fitness training arranged with a little cash

parts.note: PE is physical education
set means arranged or fixed

explanation.surface: A fitness course organised cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' gives SET, not an anagram; the peseta was Spain's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was a modest Spanish coin, a small sum of money.

clue.text: If it's to work then steps must be taken

definitions.text: If it's to work then steps must be taken

parts.words: If it's to work then steps must be taken
parts.note: sounds like advice on getting a plan going, but describes a device that only registers when the wearer walks

explanation.surface: Advice that action is needed for a plan to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer counts paces walked, so it measures nothing unless the wearer walks.

clue.text: Refuses to admit bread's crumbly

indicators.note: crumbly bread falls apart, so its letters break up and are rearranged

parts.note: bread's supplies the letters of the word bread plus S

explanation.surface: Someone turns away crumbly bread.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar or exclude someone from entry.

clue.text: A flighty creature's petulant charge

parts.note: cross means irritable or petulant
a bill is a charge to be paid

explanation.surface: A creature whose sulky invoice is part of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' means able to fly, not capricious.
explanation.definitionFit: A finch with crossed mandible tips, a bird that flies.

clue.text: Declines sound paving material

parts.note: flags means weakens or declines
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: Something weakens into good-quality road-surfacing stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat slab of stone used for pavements.

clue.text: Short light piece of music — a mere trifle

explanation.surface: A brief jaunty composition dismissed as unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief light composition, often for piano, and a thing of little importance.

clue.text: To call back could be a bloomer!

indicators.note: back says the word for call is read in the other direction

parts.note: to dub is to call or name

explanation.surface: Ringing someone back might be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder; here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bud opens into a flower, so it is a future blossom.

clue.text: A boy's height

explanation.surface: How tall a lad is.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, and a Scottish word for a mountain peak.

clue.text: A bird needs stuffing from the rear end

indicators.note: reading from the rear end means starting at the last letter and going backwards

parts.note: wad is padding or stuffing

explanation.surface: A bird being prepared for roasting by stuffing it from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The jackdaw is the bird, though the surface suggests cooking poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackdaw, a small member of the crow family.

clue.text: Being about fifty relax and let go

parts.note: re means concerning or about
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ease means relax

explanation.surface: Someone nearing fifty unwinds and lets things go.
explanation.definitionFit: To free or set loose.

clue.text: A five were not well served

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ailed means were unwell

explanation.surface: A handful of people fell ill and got poor service.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'few' must be 'five' for the wordplay to give V.
explanation.definitionFit: Availed means helped or was of use, i.e. served a purpose.

clue.text: Up-to date directions

parts.note: north, east and west are compass directions, abbreviated N, E and W
north, east and west are compass directions, abbreviated N, E and W
north, east and west are compass directions, abbreviated N, E and W

explanation.surface: Current instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern, recent, fresh.

clue.text: Mien too affected to show feeling

indicators.note: affected means artificially altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An affected manner used to display one's feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' signals the anagram of MIEN TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong feeling such as joy or anger.

clue.text: To put a name to almost all would be remarkable

parts.note: to sign is to put one's name to a document

indicators.note: almost means the word all is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: Getting nearly everyone to sign would be a notable feat.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means notable or striking, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Designing man and others accompanying a woman

parts.note: etc is short for et cetera, and others
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A scheming man and his friends escort a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designing' suggests scheming; it means making designs on plates.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who engraves designs into metal with acid.

clue.text: The price of liberation

parts.note: reads like a lofty political sacrifice, but means money paid to free a captive

explanation.surface: What freedom costs a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Money demanded for the release of a kidnapped person.

clue.text: Looked highly delighted, having support

explanation.surface: Someone smiling broadly because they are well backed.
explanation.definitionFit: Smiled radiantly, and fitted with a beam, a supporting timber.

clue.text: The person drawing beer without a light

indicators.note: without means outside, so the beer word goes round the light word

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A man pulling pints with no lamp to see by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests pulling a pint; it means depicting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who portrays, depicting in pictures or words.

clue.text: A fat goat?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an overweight animal is a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy fat spread on bread, and whimsically one that butts, as goats do.

clue.text: The mole is surprisingly flexible

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A remark on how supple a mole turns out to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple, nimble and graceful in movement.

clue.text: Solitary painter holding on

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the painter's name goes round the other word

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a 17th-century portrait painter in England

explanation.surface: A lone artist clinging on.
explanation.walkthrough: LELY is Sir Peter Lely, court painter to Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone, without company.

clue.text: Greek maid seen in Naples and Rome dashing about

indicators.note: seen in says the letters are visible within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Greek girl spotted rushing around Italian cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is spelt by 'and Rome da'; 'about' is a link word for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, the princess chained to a rock and rescued by Perseus.
